design_summary.purpose: Synthesizable FPGA wrapper for an external intelligent active-aerodynamics controller. The top module provides firmware-visible MMIO control/status, bounded host request/response transport, response validation, deterministic actuator command packing, and fault/status reporting without implementing surrogate inference or any physics solver.
design_summary.operating_model: Firmware programs compact CSR/MMIO registers to enable, arm, configure timeouts and clamp bounds, and provide compact request metadata. The RTL composes and emits bounded host_req traffic, accepts host_rsp traffic, validates sequence/status/age/range conditions, and only asserts cmd_valid when a response has been accepted and shaped into a deterministic packed actuator command. On reset or any invalid, stale, timeout, not-armed, or fault condition, actuator output validity is inhibited rather than substituted.

module_architecture.name: adaptive_aero_control_top
module_architecture.role: Top-level synthesizable FPGA wrapper and integration point.
responsibilities: Expose a firmware-visible CSR/MMIO interface for configuration and status.
Integrate bounded host request transport and bounded host response acceptance.
Forward compact request metadata to request composition.
Receive compact host response data and forward it into validation and command shaping flow.
Drive packed actuator output and cmd_valid only when validation succeeds.
Aggregate and present compact fault status for software observability.
Ensure reset, invalid, stale, timeout, and not-armed conditions inhibit command validity.
interface_notes: Uses a single clk and active-low rst_n.
Top-level I/O remains compact and implementation-friendly.
The top-level output ports are real RTL drivers and are not tied only to child inputs.
The design contract keeps external model transport direction aligned with the mandatory request/response rule.
ownership_notes: ctrl_rdata and ctrl_ready are driven by the MMIO block.
host_req_valid and host_req_data are driven by transport.
aero_cmd_out and cmd_valid are driven by the command shaper.
fault_out is driven by the fault manager.

module_architecture.name: adaptive_aero_control_top_mmio
module_architecture.role: Firmware-visible CSR/MMIO register decode and readback block.
responsibilities: Decode 64-bit MMIO writes into semantic configuration outputs.
Return 64-bit MMIO readback words for configuration and live status.
Expose live status and fault summary inputs to firmware through readback.
Provide semantic request metadata outputs for transport composition.
Ensure every declared register is reachable through RTL decode.
interface_notes: Implements the control/status window described by register_contract.
Writable fields include enable, arm, clear_faults, request_sequence, response_sequence, timeout_threshold, clamp_min, clamp_max, and compact request metadata fields.
Read-only fields reflect live busy, valid_response, stale_data, timeout, invalid_response, last_sequence, last_fault_code, response_age, and latched fault summary.
ownership_notes: Owns the software-visible control plane semantics for configuration and readback.
Is the sole software-visible source of the declared registers and fields.
Does not model inaccessible internal state as software-visible storage.

module_architecture.name: adaptive_aero_control_top_transport
module_architecture.role: Host request/response transport and transaction sequencing block.
responsibilities: Compose the compact model-request frame.
Maintain request valid until host_req_ready or local timeout abort.
Track expected and last-seen sequence numbers.
Count response age against timeout_threshold.
Qualify response availability and report transaction faults.
Provide transport-side last sequence and fault summary for software readback.
interface_notes: host_req_valid is an output and remains asserted until accepted or aborted by timeout policy.
host_req_data is a fixed-width packed request word containing only compact metadata such as sequence, operating-point ID, velocity setpoint, geometry hash/handle, and flow summary.
host_rsp_valid is received as an input and host_rsp_ready is driven as an output in accordance with the required transport direction contract.

The block exposes tx_busy, tx_expected_sequence, tx_request_issued, tx_response_valid, tx_response_sequence, tx_response_age, tx_timeout_fault, tx_stale_fault, tx_invalid_response_fault, tx_last_sequence, and tx_last_fault_code.
ownership_notes: Owns bounded transport state for one active request at a time.
Does not carry bulk tensors, geometry arrays, or flow fields on the transport path.

module_architecture.name: adaptive_aero_control_top_validation
module_architecture.role: Response validation and safety filter block.
responsibilities: Verify response sequence and transaction state alignment.
Check response status codes and reject invalid status values.
Reject expired or stale responses.
Clamp the candidate output target to configured min/max limits.
Forward only validated target, rate-limit, and mode fields to command shaping.
Generate explicit validation fault indicators for status and software recovery.
interface_notes: Requires active transaction state, matching expected sequence, acceptable response status, and non-expired age before qualifying a response as valid.
Produces validated_target, validated_rate_limit, and validated_mode_bits for the command shaper.
Generates validation_fault_invalid_response, validation_fault_stale_data, validation_fault_timeout, and validation_fault_not_armed as explicit status signals.
ownership_notes: Owns the safety filter that decides whether a host response may influence actuator command shaping.
Does not silently substitute an alternate command; it only qualifies or rejects the response.

module_architecture.name: adaptive_aero_control_top_command_shaper
module_architecture.role: Deterministic actuator command packing and saturation block.
responsibilities: Pack the final actuator command word in a deterministic format.
Apply saturation to the validated target using configured limits.
Propagate validated rate-limit and mode bits into the packed command encoding.
Provide explicit command-valid indication only for accepted responses.
Keep output deterministic and synthesis-friendly.
interface_notes: Produces aero_cmd_out as a packed actuator command word with target/deflection plus optional rate-limit and mode bits.
cmd_valid is asserted only when a validated response is available.
When no valid response exists, cmd_valid is deasserted and the command output remains inhibited.
Outputs cmd_target_sat, cmd_rate_limit_sat, and cmd_mode_bits_sat provide the saturated/packed fields used by downstream observation and validation.
ownership_notes: Does not generate a fallback or substitute command on invalid conditions.

module_architecture.name: adaptive_aero_control_top_fault_manager
module_architecture.role: Fault aggregation and status encoding block.
responsibilities: Aggregate validation and transport faults into compact live and latched status.
Encode a deterministic fault_out summary word.
Expose last accepted sequence and response age for software logging.
Hold faults latched until explicitly cleared under safe conditions.
Report busy and valid-response status for observability.
interface_notes: Consumes live transport and validation indicators and provides software-readable status outputs.
Produces status_busy, status_valid_response, status_stale_data, status_timeout, status_invalid_response, status_last_sequence, status_last_fault_code, status_response_age, and fault_out.
Supports explicit clear-faults control while preserving deterministic reset behavior.
ownership_notes: Owns the compact latched/live fault summary.
Does not directly drive transport or command behavior; it only reports and aggregates state.

interface_summary.intent: Provide a real firmware-visible 64-bit register window for configuration and readback.
Feed decoded control-plane settings and compact request metadata into the transport composer.
Emit bounded request traffic, receive bounded response traffic, and apply the mandated transport direction contract.
Forward transaction-qualified response metadata and transport fault context for acceptance checking.
Provide enable/arm state, expected response sequence, and clamp configuration to the safety filter.
Allow only qualified responses to drive packed actuator command generation.
Drive the top-level packed actuator command and its validity qualifier.
Expose saturated command fields for consistency observation and status closure.
Return live and latched status back to firmware through MMIO readback.
Drive the compact fault summary visible to software.

data_flow_summary.description: Firmware writes enable, arm, timeout, clamp, sequence, and compact metadata fields through the CSR/MMIO window.
The MMIO block decodes register writes into semantic control outputs and provides readback of live status and latched fault information.
The transport block composes a compact outbound request frame and asserts host_req_valid until host_req_ready is observed or a local timeout aborts the transaction.
Inbound host responses are only qualified when the transaction is active, sequence expectations match, and age remains within threshold.
The validation block checks status, sequence, age, and clamp bounds, then qualifies or rejects the response without substitution.
The command shaper packs a deterministic actuator command word and only asserts cmd_valid when a validated response exists.
The fault manager aggregates live and latched indicators into software-readable status and fault summary outputs.
On reset or any invalid, stale, timeout, or not-armed condition, command validity is inhibited and faults are reported for software handling.

clock_reset_summary.clocking: Single synchronous clock domain on clk at the declared FPGA-targeted frequency. All submodules are clocked from the same top-level clock and there are no additional top-level clock domains.
clock_reset_summary.reset_behavior: rst_n is active-low and synchronous in the operating constraints. On reset deassertion, the design clears pending requests, deasserts host_req_valid and cmd_valid, initializes timeout and age counters, clears fault flags to deterministic reset values, and leaves actuator output validity inhibited. No fallback or substitute command is asserted on reset.

integration_notes: The top-level hierarchy and module names are taken directly from DIGITAL_SPEC_JSON and are not redefined.
The control/status window is a real firmware-visible interface and register_contract is the source of truth for implemented registers and fields.
The external model transport direction contract is applied so that request valid/data are outputs and response valid/data are inputs at the RTL boundary.
All top-level outputs have real RTL drivers in the architecture description; none are described as child-only pass-throughs.
Bulk payload/history/FIFO storage, if needed in implementation, is expected to use a technology-neutral FPGA memory wrapper rather than flattened registers.
The design is FPGA-targeted and does not assume ASIC SRAM macros or a physics solver implementation.
No silent command substitution is described; invalid, stale, timeout, reset, or fault conditions inhibit cmd_valid and preserve deterministic fault reporting.
consistency_notes: No hierarchy, ports, or filenames may differ from digital_spec_json.
